parts.article:
The conquest of malaria in Italy
 
A review of Frank M Snowden's masterly history of a country's fight to eradicate a deadly disease
 
A The word 'malaria' means 'bad air' in Italian, and this terrible disease marked the life of the people of that country for thousands of years. Yet by 1962, Italy was officially declared malaria-free, and it has remained so ever since. Frank Snowden's study of this successful endeavour is a remarkable piece of historical work. Original, crystal clear, analytical and passionate, Snowden takes us to areas historians have rarely visited before.
 
B Everybody now knows that malaria is carried by mosquitoes. But in the 19th century most experts subscribed to the theory of 'miasma' or 'poisoning of the air'. Others made a link between swamps, water and malaria, but did not make the further leap towards insects. The consequence of these theories was that little was done to combat the disease before the end of that century. The situation was so serious that from a total population of 25m Italians, 11m were 'permanently at risk'. In warm, damp, malarial zones, the life expectancy of land workers was a terrifying 22.5 years. The economic impact of the disease was immense. Epidemics were blamed on people who originated from the hotter parts of Italy, given the widespread belief that malaria was hereditary.
 
C One of the first breakthroughs in the war against malaria came in 1898 when the zoologist Giovanni Battista Grassi demonstrated that the micro-organisms causing the disease were carried in the digestive tract of the mosquito. By releasing mosquitoes into rooms to drink the blood of healthy human volunteers, Grassi was able to make the direct link between the insects and the disease. Definitive proof of this theory was obtained after an extraordinary series of experiments in Italy, where healthy people were introduced into malarial zones but kept free of mosquito bites – and remained well. The recently formed Italian state at last had the necessary information to begin tackling the disease.
 
D A complicated approach was adopted, which made use of quinine – a drug obtained from tree bark which had long been used to combat fever, but was now seen as a crucial part of the war on malaria. Italy introduced a quinine law and a quinine tax in 1904, and the drug was administered to large numbers of rural workers. Despite its often terrible side effects, the drug was successful in limiting the spread of the disease, and in breaking cycles of infection. In addition, Italy set up rural health centres and invested heavily in education programmes. Malaria, as Snowden shows, was not just a medical problem, but a social and regional issue, and could only be defeated through multi-layered strategies.
 
E It was originally decided to give quinine to all those in vulnerable regions – even healthy people. However, peasants were often suspicious of medicine being forced upon them, and doctors were frequently met with hostility and stubborn refusal to accept the treatment offered. But despite the refusals, the strategy as a whole was hugely successful. Deaths from malaria fell by some 80% in the first decade of the 20th century and some areas escaped altogether from the scourge of the disease.
 
F The 1915-18 war delayed the campaign, as funds were diverted to the battlefields. In the 1920s and 1930s the draining of the damp, unhealthy marshlands around Rome had a certain impact on the spread of malaria. However, as war swept through the drained lands in the 1940s, the disease returned with a vengeance. Yet the country's leading malariologist Alberto Missiroli refused to order the distribution of quinine, so allowing the epidemic to spread unchecked. According to Snowden, he did this in order to create the ideal conditions for a new strategy, supported by the US Rockefeller Foundation – a massive experiment involving the extermination of mosquitoes with the chemical DDT. It is estimated that more than a third of the inhabitants in the affected area contracted malaria and countless thousands died.
 
G With the end of the war in 1945, the US government and the Rockefeller Foundation were free to experiment. DDT was sprayed from the air, and 3m Italians had their bodies covered with the chemical. The effects were immense, and by 1962 malaria was more or less gone from the whole country. One of the final victims to die of the disease in Italy was the popular cyclist, Fausto Coppi. He had contracted malaria in Africa in 1960, and the failure of doctors in Italy to spot the disease was a sign of the times. A few decades earlier, they would have immediately noticed the telltale signs; it was later claimed that a small dose of quinine would have saved his life.
 
H As there are still more than 1m deaths every year from malaria worldwide, Snowden's book also has contemporary relevance. This is a disease that affects every level of the societies where it is rampant. The economic miracle of the 1950s and 1960s which made Italy into a modern industrial nation would not have been possible without the eradication of malaria. Moreover, this book convincingly argues that the disease was 'an integral part of the big picture of modern Italian history'. This magnificent study, beautifully written and impeccably documented, deserves an audience beyond specialists in history, or in Italy.

Malaria in 19th-century Italy
Up until the late nineteenth century, experts failed to make the connection between malaria and . The most popular belief at the time was the theory, which upheld the idea that diseases were carried by unclean air. Another common idea was that malaria was a disease, and as a result people from certain parts of the country were often held responsible for the spread of epidemics. Malaria was particularly widespread in rural regions, where could be extremely short.

reference:
Q14

解析 题目说直到19世纪末，专家们未能建立疟疾与____之间的联系。原文B段提到有些人将沼泽、水和疟疾联系起来，但“did not make the further leap towards insects（没有进一步联想到昆虫）”，填 insects。

干扰 虽然我们知道是蚊子（mosquitoes），但原文在此处特指未能跨越到“昆虫”这一概念，且蚊子也是昆虫的一种。

句子 Everybody now knows that malaria is carried by mosquitoes. But in the 19th century most experts subscribed to the theory of 'miasma' or 'poisoning of the air'. Others made a link between swamps, water and malaria, but did not make the further leap towards insects. The consequence of these theories was that little was done to combat the disease before the end of that century.

Q15

解析 题目说当时最流行的信念是____理论，该理论支持疾病由不洁空气传播。原文B段提到大多数专家认同“theory of 'miasma' or 'poisoning of the air'（瘴气理论或空气中毒）”，填 miasma。

干扰 “Unclean air” 对应 “poisoning of the air”，理论名称为 miasma。

句子 But in the 19th century most experts subscribed to the theory of 'miasma' or 'poisoning of the air'.

Q16

解析 题目说另一个普遍的想法是疟疾是一种____疾病。原文B段末尾提到流行病被归咎于来自意大利较热地区的人，鉴于广泛认为“malaria was hereditary（疟疾是遗传的）”，填 hereditary。

干扰 “Held responsible” 对应 “blamed on”，原因是认为它是 hereditary。

句子 Epidemics were blamed on people who originated from the hotter parts of Italy, given the widespread belief that malaria was hereditary.

Q17

解析 题目说疟疾在农村地区尤为普遍，在那里的____可能极短。原文B段提到在疟疾地区，土地工人的“life expectancy（预期寿命）”是可怕的22.5岁（即极短），填 life expectancy。

干扰 “Extremely short” 对应 “terrifying 22.5 years”。

句子 In warm, damp, malarial zones, the life expectancy of land workers was a terrifying 22.5 years.

Q18

解析 题目说Giovanni Battista Grassi研究中的志愿者来自意大利的所有地区（all parts）。原文C段只提到“healthy human volunteers（健康的人类志愿者）”，并未提及他们来自哪里，信息缺失，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 不要因为文章讲的是意大利就默认志愿者来自全国各地。

句子 One of the first breakthroughs in the war against malaria came in 1898 when the zoologist Giovanni Battista Grassi demonstrated that the micro-organisms causing the disease were carried in the digestive tract of the mosquito. By releasing mosquitoes into rooms to drink the blood of healthy human volunteers, Grassi was able to make the direct link between the insects and the disease.

Q19

解析 题目说意大利的实验证明，即使在疟疾区，保持健康也是可能的。原文C段提到确凿证据来自于实验：健康人被带入疟疾区但“kept free of mosquito bites – and remained well（由于没被蚊子咬而保持了健康）”，选 TRUE。

干扰 “Remain healthy” 对应 “remained well”，“despite being in malarial zones” 对应 “introduced into malarial zones”。

句子 Definitive proof of this theory was obtained after an extraordinary series of experiments in Italy, where healthy people were introduced into malarial zones but kept free of mosquito bites – and remained well.

Q20

解析 题目说在20世纪初，奎宁被成功地给到了脆弱地区的所有居民（all inhabitants）。原文E段说虽然最初**决定（decided）**给所有人，但农民经常怀疑并“stubborn refusal to accept（顽固拒绝接受）”，所以并没有成功给到“所有”人，选 FALSE。

干扰 “Successfully administered to all” 与原文的 “refusal to accept” 矛盾。

句子 It was originally decided to give quinine to all those in vulnerable regions – even healthy people. However, peasants were often suspicious of medicine being forced upon them, and doctors were frequently met with hostility and stubborn refusal to accept the treatment offered. But despite the refusals, the strategy as a whole was hugely successful.

Q21

解析 题目提到显示抗疟疾药物计划显著结果的数据（figure）。原文E段提到在使用奎宁策略后，“Deaths from malaria fell by some 80%（疟疾死亡人数下降了约80%）”，80%即具体数据，选 E。

干扰 “Figure” 对应 “80%”，“Dramatic results” 对应 “fell by some 80% / hugely successful”。

句子 But despite the refusals, the strategy as a whole was hugely successful. Deaths from malaria fell by some 80% in the first decade of the 20th century and some areas escaped altogether from the scourge of the disease.

Q22

解析 题目提到关于疟疾如何传播的重要发现。原文C段提到Grassi证明了微生物是“carried in the digestive tract of the mosquito（由蚊子消化道携带）”并直接联系了昆虫和疾病，这是关于传播方式的突破性发现，选 C。

干扰 “How malaria is spread” 对应 “carried in... mosquito... link between insects and the disease”。

句子 One of the first breakthroughs in the war against malaria came in 1898 when the zoologist Giovanni Battista Grassi demonstrated that the micro-organisms causing the disease were carried in the digestive tract of the mosquito. By releasing mosquitoes into rooms to drink the blood of healthy human volunteers, Grassi was able to make the direct link between the insects and the disease.

Q23

解析 题目提到一位专家决定不阻止疾病传播。原文F段提到主要疟疾学家Alberto Missiroli“refused to order the distribution of quinine, so allowing the epidemic to spread unchecked（拒绝下令分发奎宁，从而任由流行病肆虐）”，选 F。

干扰 “Decision not to halt” 对应 “refused to order... allowing... to spread”。

句子 Yet the country's leading malariologist Alberto Missiroli refused to order the distribution of quinine, so allowing the epidemic to spread unchecked. According to Snowden, he did this in order to create the ideal conditions for a new strategy, supported by the US Rockefeller Foundation – a massive experiment involving the extermination of mosquitoes with the chemical DDT.

Q24

解析 题目提到疟疾故事对当今读者的意义。原文H段开头说由于全球每年仍有超百万人死于疟疾，Snowden的书具有“contemporary relevance（当代相关性/现实意义）”，选 H。

干扰 “Significance for today” 对应 “contemporary relevance”。

句子 As there are still more than 1m deaths every year from malaria worldwide, Snowden's book also has contemporary relevance. This is a disease that affects every level of the societies where it is rampant.

Q25

解析 题目提到阻碍科学理解疟疾的错误假设的例子。原文B段提到19世纪专家信奉“miasma（瘴气）”理论或认为疟疾是“hereditary（遗传的）”，这些导致了“little was done（无所作为）”，即阻碍了理解和防治，选 B。

干扰 “False assumptions” 对应 “theory of 'miasma' / belief that malaria was hereditary”。

句子 But in the 19th century most experts subscribed to the theory of 'miasma' or 'poisoning of the air'. Others made a link between swamps, water and malaria, but did not make the further leap towards insects. The consequence of these theories was that little was done to combat the disease before the end of that century.

Q26

解析 题目提到支持抗击疟疾斗争的立法参考。原文D段提到意大利在1904年引入了“quinine law（奎宁法）”，即立法，选 D。

干扰 “Legislation” 对应 “law”。

句子 A complicated approach was adopted, which made use of quinine – a drug obtained from tree bark which had long been used to combat fever, but was now seen as a crucial part of the war on malaria. Italy introduced a quinine law and a quinine tax in 1904, and the drug was administered to large numbers of rural workers.
